pages.name: Undo the flow
pages.text: A [[flow diagram]] shows what is done to x, in order. In 3(x − 2) = 27 the bracket keeps x − 2 together, so 2 is taken away first, then the whole of it is multiplied by 3. Undo it from the right, 27 ÷ 3 = 9 and 9 + 2 = 11, then put 11 back in to check.

pages.name: Cable runs
pages.task: Four circuits each take a run of x metres plus 3 m extra at the ends, 32 m of cable in all. Solve 4(x + 3) = 32.
pages.why: The flow diagram is x, then + 3, then × 4, giving 32. Undo it from the right: 32 ÷ 4 = 8 m a circuit, and 8 − 3 = 5. So each run is 5 m, and 4(5 + 3) = 32.

pages.name: Expand first
pages.text: Expanding first works too, as expanding does not change the value. 3(x − 2) = 27 is the same equation as 3x − 6 = 27, so add 6 to both sides, then divide by 3. Both routes give x = 11.

pages.task: Look at the structure first. Dividing both sides by 5 first suits only one of these. Which one?
pages.why: In 5(x + 1) = 35 the 5 multiplies the whole left side, so ÷ 5 gives x + 1 = 7 and x = 6. In 5(x + 1) + x = 35 the lone x sits outside the bracket, so ÷ 5 would turn it into x ÷ 5. Expand that one first: 6x + 5 = 35, so x = 5.

pages.task: In 3(x + 4) + 2x = 37 the 3 multiplies only the bracket, so expand first. What does the left side collect to?
pages.why: The 3 multiplies both terms in the bracket, making 3x + 12, and 3x and 2x are like terms, making 5x. So 5x + 12 = 37, 5x = 25 and x = 5. Dividing both sides by 3 first would turn the 2x into 2x ÷ 3.

pages.name: The bar is a bracket
pages.text: A fraction bar holds everything above it together, the way a bracket does. So in (x + 4) ÷ 3 = 5 the 4 is added first, then the whole of x + 4 is divided by 3. Undo it from the right, 5 × 3 = 15 and 15 − 4 = 11.

pages.name: Undo in order
pages.task: Solve (x − 2) ÷ 4 = 3 by undoing the flow diagram.
pages.why: The flow diagram is x, then − 2, then ÷ 4, giving 3. Undo it from the right: 3 × 4 = 12, and 12 + 2 = 14. Check: (14 − 2) ÷ 4 = 3.

pages.name: Two fractions
pages.text: With two fractions, multiply every term on both sides by the [[least common denominator]], the smallest number both bottom numbers divide into (UK books call it the lowest common multiple). For x ÷ 2 + x ÷ 3 = 10 that is 6, and 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 6 halves of x make 3x, and 6 thirds of x make 2x. The 10 becomes 60 too, so 5x = 60 and x = 12.

pages.name: One more
pages.why: The 5 multiplies x and − 1, and the minus changes x + 3 to − x − 3. So 5x − 5 − x − 3 = 20, which is 4x − 8 = 20, so 4x = 28 and x = 7. Check: 30 − 10 = 20.
